papers.title: On the Design of a Slow Control Interlock System for the European GateMate FPGA
authors: Vitalii Burtsev, Daniele Passaretti, Daniel Anders, Christof Pfannenmueller, Fabian Lurz, Thilo Pionteck
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32275v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slow Control Systems (SCSs) are essential for the monitoring, configuration, and protection of distributed safety-critical systems in scientific, industrial, and medical applications. Although software-based SCS architectures offer flexibility and scalability, they suffer from software aging and non-deterministic latencies, which limit long-term reliability and timely reaction to critical errors, often requiring additional hardware interlock systems. This paper presents an FPGA-centric lightweight Slow Control Interlock System (SCIS) designed to achieve deterministic ultra-low-latency reaction times in long-running dependable systems. papers.title: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Exposing Its Security Risks
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.23022v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: GPUs are the main platform for large-scale machine learning and power the largest supercomputers. Their load/store units (LSUs) often determine kernel performance and have been exploited in prior attacks. Yet what is known about the LSU is only a few isolated mechanisms and parameters, and even a single one has been enough for an attack. In particular, it is still unknown what a load costs, where loads contend, and even whether a warp can starve due to contention. Until each is measured, neither its security risk nor a defense is known. We reverse-engineer how the LSU serves load instructions on recent NVIDIA GPUs with microbenchmarks and analyze the security implications. papers.title: Discovering Bandwidth-Efficient Prefetchers to Shrink the Cache Hierarchy
authors: Patrick Tser Jern Kon, Akanksha Jain, Abraham Gonzalez, Rui Meng, Dilara Soylu, Shubham Agarwal, Yawen Wang, Iman Hosseini, Hanna Alam, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister, Nanyun Peng, Chun-Liang Li, Parthasarathy Ranganathan
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31983v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Shared last-level caches (LLCs) increasingly dominate server processor die area, forcing architects to trade core counts for cache capacity. While intelligent data prefetching offers a pathway to reclaim this silicon, designing coordinated, multi-level prefetching policies for multi-core systems is bottlenecked by day-long, cycle-level simulations. This simulation wall limits even LLM-based microarchitecture discovery; the state-of-the-art ArchAgent system evolves one cache level at a time on single-core benchmarks, adds multi-core configurations only at the end, and trails the human champion under multi-core shared cache contention. papers.title: Walk the Cycle: An Efficient Stochastic Solver for Periodic Thermal Analysis of 2.5D/3D ICs
authors: Shengnan Cai, Qibo Xue, Tianshu Hou, Tianxiang Zhu, Zixiao Wang, Yibo Lin, Runsheng Wang, Bei Yu
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32082v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-term periodic thermal analysis is essential for designing 2.5D/3D ICs operating under periodic workloads. Deterministic global solvers can be costly for repeated thermal queries, while existing random-walk methods are not tailored to long-term periodic problems or multiscale 3D IC structures, limiting their efficiency and accuracy. We propose CycleWalker, a periodic residual random-walk solver. First, we formulate the periodic steady state (PSS) as an infinite-history backward walk, which needs no initial temperature or warm-up but charges the full temperature field to every path. papers.title: Lachesis: Lifetime-Aware KV Cache Placement for Agent Serving across HBM and High-Bandwidth Flash
authors: Jaehoon Yang, Jeongmin Lee, Haneul Park, Seung Yul Lee, Nam Sung Kim, Jae W. Lee
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.08378v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In agent serving, agents and their sub-agents accumulate context as KV cache across many requests, far beyond HBM capacity. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) adds greater capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth, allowing a server to grow its batch and throughput under a relaxed SLO. We show that this gain meets an endurance wall as the batch growth wears HBF out within its warranty period. Prior work analyzes which KV should reach HBF assuming a request's KV remains readable until completion. However, an agent run is stateful, and by design, its harness discards parts of the context throughout the run. papers.title: DELTA: Diagnosing Exploration Lineages via Twin-path Alignment - What Can Contrasting Design Paths Reveal About Microarchitectural Behavior?
authors: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Darsh Asher, Bita Aslrousta, Amna Hassan, Debayan Sengupta, Azam Ghanbari, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31767v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Architects have two mature instruments for performance work. Top-Down analysis tells them where a design loses its pipeline slots, and design-space exploration (DSE) tells them which configuration scores best. Neither explains why a search stops improving: why a backend-bound design rejects a prefetcher that the bottleneck label recommends, or why a capacity increase that helped in one configuration hurts in the next. This paper argues that the evidence needed to answer such questions is already produced during exploration and then discarded. papers.title: MOSAIC: Memory-Organized Search with Anti-Imitation Crossover for Training-Free Microarchitecture Optimization
authors: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Bita Aslrousta, Paula Contreras, Azam Ghanbari, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models can generate cache-replacement policies. The central challenge is to retain performance on workloads excluded from the search. In our adaptations of published search methods, generated code resembles established policies, with cosine similarities of 0.78-0.84. The wider comparison also shows held-out harmonic-mean instructions-per-cycle (IPC) losses of 1.0-2.4%. We present MOSAIC, a search controller that improves policies without updating language-model weights. It stores concise lessons from previous evaluations rather than repeatedly copying high-scoring code. papers.title: Scaling Architectural Simulation to Giga Instructions Per Second
authors: Zhouyi Shen, Hao Tang, Ruike Liu, Jingwei Sun, Guangzhong Sun
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32397v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The cost of detailed architectural simulation constrains design-space exploration, while parallelization across simulated cores offers limited host concurrency for single-core and small multicore targets. We present GIPSim, an instruction-driven simulator that derives instruction timing from dependencies and resource constraints, reducing the overhead of updating pipeline state every simulated cycle. It applies synchronization-guided temporal decomposition to recorded execution, exposing host parallelism beyond the target core count.
